newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-NANTES LOSE $10 MILLION OVER TWO YEARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NANTES LOSE $10 MILLION OVER TWO YEARS.

text.p: French first division club Nantes have suffered total losses of 52 million francs ($10 million) over the last two years, city mayor Jean-Marc Ayrault said on Thursday.

Ayrault said it was extremely difficult to obtain complete information on the club's finances, which he said was "the fruit of strange management in these last years" -- a remark aimed at former president Guy Scherrer, who resigned a year ago.

Ayrault said he had asked Nantes, who won the French league championship with a brilliant young team in 1995, "to sell as many players as necessary before the end of June with a view to covering the deficit as quickly as possible".

Nantes have gone a long way towards this with the transfers of Chadian forward Japhet N'Doram and defender Christophe Pignol to champions Monaco for 20 and 15 million francs ($4 and $3 million) respectively and midfielder Claude Makelele to Marseille for 13 million francs ($2.5 million).
But the result of a second major exodus after the break-up of the championship side which reached the 1996 European Cup semifinals is that coach Jean-Claude Suaudeau faces another rebuilding job.
Last season his side went the first 10 league matches without winning but then embarked on an unbeaten run which went to 30 matches and put them in third place in the final first division standings.
